stem: Which anthropometric trend would most strongly suggest ongoing diarrhoea or malabsorption in a child at review?

options.text: Weight continues to fall while head circumference remains maintained
Weight and height fall together with normal head circumference
Weight, height, and head circumference all fall together
Head circumference begins crossing centiles despite previously normal values
Height alone falls with stable weight and head circumference

explanation: Weight continues to fall while head circumference remains maintained. This pattern most strongly suggests ongoing increased loss such as diarrhoea or malabsorption, with head growth relatively preserved.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because persistent weight faltering with preserved head circumference is a classic pattern for chronic gastrointestinal loss such as diarrhoea or malabsorption.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because simultaneous weight and height faltering with a normal head circumference is less specific and more suggestive of broader growth issues such as constitutional or endocrine causes.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because reduced weight, height, and head circumference together suggests a more global process, including possible intrauterine or genetic causes.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because head circumference crossing centiles is not the typical pattern for chronic diarrhoea or malabsorption and should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because isolated height faltering with stable weight does not fit the classic pattern of chronic gastrointestinal loss described here.
